course.name: Salon & Spa Management Workforce Development Program
course.subject: salon_spa_management
course.prerequisite_policy: Open-course enrollment; prerequisites and learner eligibility may be configured by the provider.

course_learning_outcomes: Demonstrate industry-standard sanitation, disinfection, and infection-control practices.
Apply workplace safety and client-protection procedures.
Understand anatomy, physiology, chemistry, electricity, and other sciences applicable to their pathway.
Recognize contraindications and determine when a service should not be performed.
Select appropriate products, tools, equipment, and procedures.
Interpret professional terminology and service procedures.
Apply state laws, regulations, professional ethics, and scope-of-practice requirements.
Prepare for applicable state and/or NIC examinations.
Develop marketing, sales, financial-literacy, and entrepreneurship skills.
Build a professional portfolio and career plan.
Demonstrate readiness for employment, apprenticeship, entrepreneurship, and advanced training.

weeks.title: PHASE I — PROFESSIONAL FOUNDATIONS — Week 1
weeks.focus: Salon and spa industry overview
weeks.instructor_overview: This week develops salon and spa industry overview through explicit instruction, instructor modelling, guided analysis, supervised practice, and independent application. Learners connect the concepts to the salon and spa practice, explain why the procedures matter, and demonstrate the expected safe and professional approach. Emphasize infection control, client protection, professional service, and regulatory compliance.

program_overview: Salon & Spa Management Workforce Development Program
36-Week Career Training, Licensure Preparation & Industry Certification Program
Three Specialized Career Pathways
1. Cosmetology | 2. Esthetics | 3. Nail Technology
Learn the Profession. Master the Skills. Pass the Exam. Build the Career.
Program Summary

The Salon & Spa Management Workforce Development Program is a comprehensive 36-week career preparation program designed to provide students with foundational salon and spa business knowledge while allowing each participant to specialize in one of three professional pathways:
Cosmetology
Esthetics
Nail Technology

The program integrates professional theory, practical competencies, safety and infection control, client services, business and salon management, entrepreneurship, employability skills, state licensing preparation, NIC-aligned examination preparation, realistic practical simulations, quizzes, module examinations, AI-powered instruction, and individualized intervention.

NIC currently provides national Theory, Practical, and Written Practical examinations across cosmetology-related professions, including Cosmetology, Esthetics, and Nail Technology. However, individual states and jurisdictions determine their own licensing requirements and may use different examinations or state-specific requirements. Therefore, the program's final licensure-preparation component should be customized to the student's licensing jurisdiction.
Program Mission

The mission of the Salon & Spa Management Workforce Development Program is to develop technically competent, safety-conscious, customer-focused, business-minded, and examination-ready beauty professionals who possess the knowledge, practical competencies, professional behaviors, and entrepreneurial skills necessary to transition successfully from training to licensure and employment.
Program Goals
Students completing the program will be prepared to:
Demonstrate industry-standard sanitation, disinfection, and infection-control practices.
Apply workplace safety and client-protection procedures.
Understand anatomy, physiology, chemistry, electricity, and other sciences applicable to their pathway.
Conduct professional client consultations.
Recognize contraindications and determine when a service should not be performed.
Select appropriate products, tools, equipment, and procedures.
Demonstrate pathway-specific practical competencies.
Interpret professional terminology and service procedures.
Apply state laws, regulations, professional ethics, and scope-of-practice requirements.
Prepare for applicable state and/or NIC examinations.
Demonstrate professional customer-service competencies.
Understand salon/spa operations and management.
Develop marketing, sales, financial-literacy, and entrepreneurship skills.
Build a professional portfolio and career plan.
Demonstrate readiness for employment, apprenticeship, entrepreneurship, and advanced training.
Important Licensure Structure
The program should operate on two parallel tracks:
Track A — National/NIC-Aligned Preparation
Students receive instruction and simulations reflecting national examination competencies and commonly assessed theory and practical skills.
